vtherm_version.title: SmartPI cannot start
vtherm_version.description:
SmartPI requires Versatile Thermostat {minimum_version} or later. Installed version: {installed_version}.

SmartPI cannot start because this version is too old or could not be verified. Update Versatile Thermostat, then restart Home Assistant.

dpercent_filter.title: SmartPI valve commands are filtered for {name}
dpercent_filter.description:
The thermostat {name} controls a valve and its Versatile Thermostat "Regulation threshold" is set to {dpercent} %. Versatile Thermostat filters small changes in the opening requested by SmartPI and forces openings below the threshold to 0 %. SmartPI uses the retained opening reported by Versatile Thermostat for learning. This filtering reduces command resolution; this warning alone does not mean that learning has failed.

In the Versatile Thermostat "Underlyings" settings of {name}, use a threshold of 0 only if your device allows it. For the Sonoff TRVZB, the Versatile Thermostat documentation recommends at least 3 % to avoid a possible loss of valve calibration: keep that threshold even if this warning remains.

period_filter.title: SmartPI valve commands are delayed for {name}
period_filter.description:
The thermostat {name} controls a valve and its Versatile Thermostat "Regulation minimum period" is set to {period_min} minutes. Versatile Thermostat holds back a change of the valve command requested by SmartPI until this period has elapsed since the previous change, except when a cycle restarts. SmartPI uses the retained opening reported by Versatile Thermostat for learning, but its requested changes can be delayed. This warning alone does not mean that learning has failed.

For immediate command updates, open the Versatile Thermostat settings of {name}, go to the "Underlyings" menu and set "Regulation minimum period" to 0 only if your device allows it. Keep any period required by your device.

opening_remap.title: SmartPI valve linearization conflicts with the opening settings of {name}
opening_remap.description:
The thermostat {name} uses the SmartPI valve linearization, but its Versatile Thermostat opening settings ("Opening threshold degree", "Min opening degrees", "Max opening degrees" or "Max closing degree") remap the opening before it reaches the valve. SmartPI inverts its valve curve on a value that is no longer the physical valve opening, so its model is learned on a wrong command.

To fix it, either disable the valve linearization in the SmartPI settings of {name}, or restore the default Versatile Thermostat opening settings (threshold 0, minimum 0, maximum 100, max closing 100) only if your device allows it. With direct valve control in over_climate mode, the regulation threshold also raises the opening threshold. If your device requires a non-zero threshold, keep it and disable the SmartPI valve linearization. If the radiator only starts heating above a given opening and your device allows the default Versatile Thermostat opening settings, set that opening as "Minimum valve opening" in the SmartPI valve curve.
